title: Humanoid
summary: The 'alive' component of characters: health, movement (WalkSpeed, JumpPower), states (running, swimming), Died event, and character controls like MoveTo and TakeDamage. Present in every player character.

properties.name: Health / MaxHealth
properties.description: Current/maximum health. Health <= 0 kills the character (Died fires).

properties.name: JumpPower / JumpHeight / UseJumpPower
properties.description: Jump strength — either power or height mode.

properties.name: MoveDirection
properties.description: Direction the character is currently trying to move (read-only-ish).

properties.name: AutoRotate
properties.description: Whether the character turns to face movement direction.

events.name: Died
events.description: Fires when health reaches 0. THE standard death hook — but it fires once and the Humanoid is then dead.

events.name: HealthChanged
events.description: Fires on every health change — great for health bars.

events.name: StateChanged
events.description: Movement/state transitions: Running, Jumping, Swimming, Climbing, Dead…

methods.name: MoveTo
methods.description: NPC walking: instructs the character to walk toward a point. Fires MoveToFinished when it arrives (or gives up).

methods.name: Jump
methods.description: Setting the Jump property to true makes the character jump.

methods.name: LoadAnimation
methods.description: Legacy path; prefer Animator:LoadAnimation via the Animator object.

explanation.whatItIs: The brain-and-vitals object inside every character model: it's what makes a pile of parts a living, walking, damageable character.
explanation.whyItExists: Characters share enormous behavior — health, walking, jumping, dying. Humanoid packages all of it once.
whenToUse: Damage: TakeDamage or Health math on the server (authoritative!)
whenNotToUse: Client-authoritative damage — clients must request, servers must decide
Non-character objects — they don't need a Humanoid
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Character (Model)
 ├─ Humanoid          ← health, movement, death
 ├─ HumanoidRootPart  ← the anchor part
 ├─ Animator          ← animation playback
 └─ body parts…

No Humanoid → not a character.
Health 0 → Died → respawn handling.
```
tips: Characters respawn: reconnect Died each time via CharacterAdded, not once per player
Find the humanoid with character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") — name lookups can fail
ForceField (spawn protection) blocks TakeDamage — check before expecting damage
NPC pathing: pair MoveTo with PathfindingService for obstacles
commonMistakes: Applying damage from a LocalScript and trusting it — exploiters will heal themselves
Expecting Died to fire again after respawn — new character = new Humanoid
Setting Health on the client — it replicates poorly and isn't authoritative
Forgetting MoveTo can fail/time out — always listen to MoveToFinished

examples.title: Server-side damage + death handling
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local function setupCharacter(player, character)
    local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

    humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
        print(player.Name .. " died")
        -- leaderstats, kill feed, respawn logic, etc.
    end)

    humanoid.HealthChanged:Connect(function(health)
        -- e.g. replicate to a custom health bar
    end)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        setupCharacter(player, character)
    end)
end)

examples.title: Simple NPC patrol with MoveTo
examples.code:
local npc = workspace.NPC
local humanoid = npc:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local waypoints = workspace.PatrolPoints:GetChildren()
local i = 1

while humanoid.Health > 0 do
    local target = waypoints[i]
    humanoid:MoveTo(target.Position)
    humanoid.MoveToFinished:Wait()   -- wait until arrived/timeout
    i = i % #waypoints + 1
end
